clue.text: Twice divulge information in a club, say

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: Someone gives away secrets twice over while at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' tells you the one phrase is used for both pieces. In bridge, a lone card of a suit in a hand, such as a single club, has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games a lone card held in a suit is so called, and a club is one example.

clue.text: Do without women

parts.note: reads like managing without women, but do means a party, here one for men only

explanation.surface: Someone manages without any women around.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a do is a party; this one, for a groom before his wedding, is men only.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor celebration held by the groom's male friends is a party that excludes women.

clue.text: Loop-line quickly going North, then East

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: soon means before long, quickly
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A loop of railway track runs fast northwards and then turns east.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope tied in a running knot forms a loop, the line being the rope.

clue.text: Women who saw wartime service in the field

definitions.text: Women who saw wartime service in the field

parts.words: Women who saw wartime service in the field
parts.note: reads like women on the battlefield, but the field is a farmer's field

explanation.surface: Women served at the front in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Land Army was a British organisation in both world wars that sent women to work on farms.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime body of British women farm workers did their service on the land.

clue.text: Match-box trial

parts.note: a test is an international cricket match
a case is a box or container

explanation.surface: A matchbox is being tried out.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action that sets a precedent for others is a trial of the principle.

clue.text: Observing what comes from a dumb-bell?

parts.note: a dumb bell makes no sound, so no
a ting is the sound a small bell makes

explanation.surface: Someone watches what a piece of gym equipment produces.
explanation.walkthrough: The dumb-bell of the gym is read as a dumb bell, one that gives no ting.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticing or remarking something is observing it.

clue.text: Bad spelling, possibly, in Daily Mail's leader

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Mail's is taken

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editorial column is full of misspellings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily Mail' looks like the newspaper, but Daily is a char, a British name for a cleaning lady. 'spelling' is the casting of a spell, not orthography.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic formula or incantation casts a spell, which may be malign.

clue.text: Talented number of Romans heading for the bar

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a lever is a bar used to prise

explanation.surface: A gifted group of Italians makes for the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gifted or skilful is bright and able.

clue.text: Support, from chair, fuss about sick animal

parts.note: the arm of a chair supports your elbow

indicators.note: about means going round, so the fuss surrounds the sickness

parts.note: ado means fuss
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone leans on a chair and makes a fuss about a sick pet.
explanation.definitionFit: This American mammal is armoured with bony plates.

clue.text: He keeps on accumulating endless unhappiness

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: misery is great unhappiness

explanation.surface: A man goes on piling up his woes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder of money keeps amassing wealth without spending it.

clue.text: Not a sum that's incorrect — sums

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are wrong as they stand and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher marks an answer as no sum at all because it is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums of money are quantities or totals, used here as a plural noun.

clue.text: It doesn't normally contain mother's ruin!

definitions.text: It doesn't normally contain mother's ruin!

indicators.note: to ruin the word is to wreck its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that is usually free of gin, the drink called mother's ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's ruin' is British slang for gin; a vacuum flask usually holds tea or coffee. 'ruin' also tells you to rearrange the letters of mother's.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum flask keeps hot drinks hot, so its usual contents are tea or soup, not spirits.

clue.text: Work religiously done in PE abroad

annotationWithheld.why: Work religiously done in PE abroad (5), as printed for PIETA: no parse found for 'PE abroad' giving the letters
annotationWithheld.clue: Work religiously done in PE abroad

clue.text: One who tries to steer a boat

parts.note: to con a ship is to direct its steering
a tender is a small boat serving a larger ship

explanation.surface: A novice tries to steer a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor is someone who tries for a prize.

clue.text: Are at sea in storm, breaking at last

indicators.note: one scrambled word goes inside the other
the word storm is broken up into a new order
at sea means confused, so the letters of Are are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sailors are out on the ocean as a gale breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams, one nested in the other: 'Are at sea' reads like a sailing picture but supplies jumbled fodder, and 'at last' is the definition, not a timing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The hindmost position is reached last of all.

clue.text: Missile base and plant

parts.note: an arrow is a missile shot from a bow
a root is a base or foundation

explanation.surface: A rocket base and a factory are both military sites.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical herb whose starch is used in cooking is a plant.

clue.text: Sign on the staff

parts.note: reads like joining a company's employees, but the staff is the five-line musical stave and the sign fixes the pitch

explanation.surface: Joining the workforce of a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical symbol at the start of a stave shows which note each line stands for.

clue.text: Their bank accounts are often overdrawn

definitions.text: Their bank accounts are often overdrawn

parts.words: Their bank accounts are often overdrawn
parts.note: reads like people in debt, but the bank is a riverbank and the accounts are tales of the catch, exaggerated

explanation.surface: Some people are always running up overdrafts.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers on the riverside are notorious for exaggerating the size of their catch.

clue.text: What's up? Nothing wrong being left-handed

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put out of order

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the matter is and is told nothing, apart from being left-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer or pitcher who leads with the left is a lefty.

clue.text: Driver of train having crossed lines

definitions.text: Driver of train having crossed lines

parts.words: Driver of train having crossed lines
parts.note: reads like a railway driver crossing tracks, but the train is a line of pack animals each bred from a cross

explanation.surface: An engine driver has gone over the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: A mule is the cross of a donkey and a horse, so its breeding lines are crossed.
explanation.definitionFit: The man who drives a string of mules is the driver of a pack train.

clue.text: Distance vehicle travels in reverse

indicators.note: a vehicle going backwards tells you to read its name from the end

parts.note: a dray is a low cart used by brewers

explanation.surface: How far a car goes while backing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Three feet make up this unit of length.

clue.text: Full of humanity?

parts.note: reads like being very humane or kind, but means crowded with people

explanation.surface: Is someone overflowing with compassion?
explanation.definitionFit: A densely inhabited place has a great many people in it.

clue.text: One is in high dudgeon, it ominously appears

indicators.note: is in tells you the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: high dudgeon is great anger, wrath
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in a towering rage appears as a menacing omen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost whose appearance foretells death is a spectre seen ominously.

clue.text: Disregard one note and no: another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
G is a musical note
re is another note, in the do-re-mi scale

explanation.surface: A clerk disregards one memo and refuses another.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no attention to something is to disregard it.

clue.text: Not functioning properly, being unqualified

parts.note: a computer that is down is not working
done right means done correctly

explanation.surface: A machine works badly because nobody trained the operator.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter or out-and-out, as in a complete lie, is unqualified in the sense of absolute.

clue.text: Reports come back up when such charges are dropped

definitions.text: Reports come back up when such charges are dropped

parts.words: Reports come back up when such charges are dropped
parts.note: reads like legal accusations withdrawn, but the charges are explosives dropped on submarines and the reports are their bangs

explanation.surface: News resurfaces once the accusations are withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Explosives set to detonate at a set level below the surface take their name from it.

clue.text: Girl's come about the advertisement, miss

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
an ad is short for advertisement

explanation.surface: A young woman has turned up in answer to a job advert, a Miss applying.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to avoid or escape it.

clue.text: Excuse for party in capital

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate, capital
Lib is short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: A politician's pretext for joining a party in the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea that you were elsewhere serves as an excuse.

clue.text: It may qualify as part of an agreement

definitions.text: It may qualify as part of an agreement

parts.words: It may qualify as part of an agreement
parts.note: reads like something earning a place in a deal, but qualify means limit, as a condition written into a contract does

explanation.surface: Something might count as a clause in a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipulation attached to a contract restricts or conditions its terms.

clue.text: Cover charge?

parts.note: reads like a restaurant's fee per diner, but means the price paid for insurance cover

explanation.surface: A restaurant adds a fee to the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The regular payment for an insurance policy buys cover.

clue.text: Signal to driver to stop — it's a hold-up

definitions.meaning: thumbing a lift asks a passing motorist to pull over

explanation.surface: A motorist is flagged down and finds it is a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb a ride halts a car, and a snag or delay is a temporary difficulty.

clue.text: Developed idea drawn from a bygone era

indicators.note: an idea developed is worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old notion has been worked up and sketched out.
explanation.definitionFit: The reign of the king who ruled from 1901 to 1910 is a period now long past.
